What will be the overall order of a reaction for which the rate expression is given as
Rate$= K [ A] \dfrac{1}{2} [ B] \dfrac{3}{2}$
questions.solution:
The order of reaction is equal to the sum of power of concentration of reactants given in the rate law.

Order of reaction = Sum of exponents of the concentration terms in rate law

For a given reaction,
$xA + yB \to Product$

According to the rate law,

Rate of reaction$= {K [ A ]}^{x}{[ B ]}^{y}$

Then the overall order of reaction= $x + y$

So, rate =$= K [ A] \dfrac{1}{2} [ B] \dfrac{3}{2}$

So, order of reaction = $\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{3}{2} = 2$

Hence,& the overall order of a reaction is second order.

This reaction is completed in $100 \mathrm{~min}$. The rate constant of this reaction at $t_1=10$ $\mathrm{min}$, is $10^{-2} \mathrm{~min}^{-1}$. What is the rate constant $\left(\right.$ in $\min ^{-1}$ ) at $t_2=20 \mathrm{~min} ?$
questions.solution:
For a first order reaction, rate constant does not depend upon concentration.
$\therefore$ Rate constant at $t_2=20 \mathrm{~min}$ also $10^{-2} \mathrm{~min}^{-1}$ (constant).
